module purpose: neorv32_slink is a bus-accessible stream-link endpoint with separate RX and TX FIFOs. It accepts incoming SLINK words into the RX FIFO, returns control/status and received data through the bus response, queues bus-written TX words with a programmable destination for transmission on the SLINK TX interface, and generates RX/TX interrupts from FIFO status.

use-case flows.value: enable, FIFO-clear, and interrupt-policy control bits written through the control register
transmit destination tag written into the route register
incoming RX item fields written into the RX FIFO and RX ready reported
control/status and routing state returned on bus reads
received payload returned from the RX FIFO and its source/last metadata latched for readback
bus-written TX item packed into the TX FIFO and driven onto the SLINK TX outputs
RX interrupt request generated from enabled RX FIFO status conditions
TX interrupt request generated from enabled TX FIFO status conditions
control state, routing state, metadata latches, and interrupt outputs forced to zero while rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.reasoning: `ctrl.enable <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_en_c)` stores the module enable bit (line 148), and reads return it at line 167. This state directly controls FIFO clearing by `rx_fifo.clear <= (not ctrl.enable) or ctrl.rx_clr` (line 226) and `tx_fifo.clear <= (not ctrl.enable) or ctrl.tx_clr` (line 294), and it gates both interrupt outputs at lines 259 and 310. Integrity is established because these implemented behaviors become incorrect if the stored enable state is corrupted; availability is also established because the bit is held until reset or rewrite.

The explicit RX-clear command is written by `ctrl.rx_clr <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_rx_clr_c)` (line 149), defaulted low each cycle at line 140, and delivered to the RX FIFO clear control by `rx_fifo.clear <= (not ctrl.enable) or ctrl.rx_clr` (line 226) through the FIFO connection at line 213. The local metadata path also reacts to clear: `if (rx_fifo.clear = '1') then rx_last <= '0';` (lines 242-243). Integrity is established because the implemented clear action must occur exactly when this request is asserted; availability is established because the module provides this clear action on demand.

The explicit TX-clear command is written by `ctrl.tx_clr <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_tx_clr_c)` (line 150), defaulted low each cycle at line 141, and delivered to the TX FIFO clear control by `tx_fifo.clear <= (not ctrl.enable) or ctrl.tx_clr` (line 294) through the FIFO connection at line 281. Integrity is established because the implemented transmit-buffer clear action must follow this stored request exactly; availability is established because the module provides this clear action on demand.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt generation policy settings for RX and TX FIFO status
conceptual assets.reasoning: Six stored control bits define which FIFO-status conditions raise interrupts: lines 152-157 write `ctrl.irq_rx_nempty`, `ctrl.irq_rx_half`, `ctrl.irq_rx_full`, `ctrl.irq_tx_empty`, `ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf`, and `ctrl.irq_tx_nfull`; lines 178-183 read them back. The RX interrupt equation consumes the RX policy bits at lines 260-262, and the TX interrupt equation consumes the TX policy bits at lines 311-313. Integrity is established because interrupt selection must match these stored policy settings; availability is established because the settings are retained until reset or rewrite.

conceptual assets.concept: Received SLINK item fields accepted for buffering and later readout
conceptual assets.reasoning: The receive path packs the incoming fields into the RX FIFO by `rx_fifo.wdata(31 downto 0) <= slink_rx_data_i` (line 230), `rx_fifo.wdata(35 downto 32) <= slink_rx_src_i` (line 231), and `rx_fifo.wdata(36) <= slink_rx_last_i` (line 232), with writes enabled by line 229. On dequeue, `rx_last <= rx_fifo.rdata(36)` (line 245) and `route_src <= rx_fifo.rdata(35 downto 32)` (line 248) capture the metadata, while the payload is returned on the transport-excluded bus response at line 191. Integrity is established because the consumer must receive the same payload/source/last fields that entered the module; the reportable structural refs here are the ingress ports and the local metadata latches, since the bus transport port is excluded.

conceptual assets.concept: Transmit SLINK item fields delivered to the TX path, including payload, destination tag and last marker
conceptual assets.reasoning: The destination tag is stored by `route_dst <= bus_req_i.data(3 downto 0)` (line 161). Each queued TX item is then formed by `tx_fifo.wdata <= bus_req_i.addr(2) & route_dst & bus_req_i.data` (line 296), so the last marker, destination tag, and payload are packed together before entering the TX FIFO at line 285. Dequeued fields leave the entity on `slink_tx_data_o <= tx_fifo.rdata(31 downto 0)` (line 299), `slink_tx_dst_o <= tx_fifo.rdata(35 downto 32)` (line 300), and `slink_tx_last_o <= tx_fifo.rdata(36)` (line 301). Integrity is established because the downstream consumer must receive exactly the queued transmit tuple; the bus request port that supplied payload and last is transport-excluded, so the reportable refs are the stored destination setting, the packed TX word, and the output ports.

`slink_rx_ready_o <= rx_fifo.free` (line 233) exports the module's decision that RX buffer space is available. Integrity is established because an upstream producer depends on this exact ready indication to know when it may deliver a word; availability is also established because the module continuously presents the current free-space decision on this port.

`slink_tx_valid_o <= tx_fifo.avail` (line 302) exports the module's decision that a TX item is available on the transmit outputs driven at lines 299-301. Integrity is established because the downstream consumer depends on this exact valid indication to interpret those outputs correctly; availability is also established because the module continuously presents the current availability decision on this port.

The module computes the RX interrupt by `rx_irq_o <= ctrl.enable and ((ctrl.irq_rx_nempty and rx_fifo.avail) or (ctrl.irq_rx_half and rx_fifo.half) or (ctrl.irq_rx_full and (not rx_fifo.free)))` (lines 259-262). Integrity is established because the reported event must match these enabled RX FIFO status conditions exactly; availability is established because the event is registered every clock when the implemented condition holds.

The module computes the TX interrupt by `tx_irq_o <= ctrl.enable and ((ctrl.irq_tx_empty and (not tx_fifo.avail)) or (ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf and (not tx_fifo.half)) or (ctrl.irq_tx_nfull and tx_fifo.free))` (lines 310-313). Integrity is established because the reported event must match these enabled TX FIFO status conditions exactly; availability is established because the event is registered every clock when the implemented condition holds.
